<x_0.0322><y_0.0305>Berlin. All his time was consecrated to some serious occupation, with the exception of one hour in the evening, which he employed in making and receiving visits. His greatest enjoyment was in cultivating his garden. A warm and strong friend, he gave many proofs of gratitude to those protectors, who had generously assisted him in his studies. He has been reproached with being irascible; but in spite of some slight blemishes, the memory of Bilfinger will be always dear to his countrymen, and honoured by all Germans. Wurtemberg reckons him among the greatest men which she has produced, and proposes him as a model to her statesmen and her men of letters. He was never married, and left no issue. He died at Stuttgart the 18th of February 1750. His works, besides various Papers published in the Me- moirs of the St Petersburg and Paris Academies of Science, are :<x_0.7402><y_0.2727><class_Text>

<x_0.0332><y_0.2812>1. _Disputatio de Harmonia præstabilità_, Tubingen, 1721, in 4to.<x_0.7266><y_0.3109><class_List-item>

<x_0.0303><y_0.3086>_2. De Harmonia Animi et Corporis Humani maxi- me præstabilità Commentatio Hypothetica_, Francfort on the Main, 1723, in 5vo. This work was inserted in the Expurgatory Index at Rome in 1734.<x_0.7295><y_0.3648><class_List-item>

<x_0.0264><y_0.3617>_3. De Origine et Permissione Mali, praccipue Moralis, Commentatio Philosophica_, ibid. 1724, in 5vo.<x_0.7246><y_0.3922><class_List-item>

<x_0.0234><y_0.3883>_4. Specimen Doctrina Veterum Sinarum Moralis et Politica_, Francf. 1724, in 4to._<x_0.7236><y_0.4172><class_List-item>

<x_0.0225><y_0.4141>_5. Dissertatio Historico-cataptrica de Speculo Ar- chimedis_, Tubingen, 1725, in 4to._<x_0.7227><y_0.4437><class_List-item>

<x_0.0215><y_0.4406>_6. Dilucidationes Philosophicae de Deo, Animal Humaná, Mundo, et Generalibus Rerum Affectionibus,_ ibid. 1725, in 4to.<x_0.7217><y_0.4828><class_List-item>

<x_0.0205><y_0.4797>_7. Bilfingeri et Holmanni Epistola de Harmonia Præstabilità, 1728, in 4to._<x_0.7207><y_0.5094><class_List-item>

<x_0.0195><y_0.5062>_8. Disputatio de Natura et Legibus Studii in Theologià Thetici,_ ibid. 1731, in 4to.<x_0.7197><y_0.5359><class_List-item>

<x_0.0518><y_0.5336>_9. Disputatio de Cultu Dei Rationali,_ ibid. 1731.<x_0.7158><y_0.55><class_List-item>

<x_0.0186><y_0.5461>10. _Notac Breves in Ben. Spinose Methodum Ex- picandi Scripturas_, Tub. 1732, in 4to.<x_0.7188><y_0.5758><class_List-item>

<x_0.0166><y_0.5727>11. _De Mysteriis Christiane Fidei Generatim Spec tatis Semno, Recittatus 1732, Tubingen, 1732, in 4to._<x_0.7168><y_0.6031><class_List-item>

<x_0.0498><y_0.5992>12. _Elementa Physics_, Leipzig, 1742, in 5vo.<x_0.6436><y_0.6156><class_List-item>

<x_0.0508><y_0.6125>13. _La Citadelle Coupée_, Leipzig, 1756, in 4to.<x_0.667><y_0.6297><class_List-item>

<x_0.0488><y_0.6359>See _Biographie Universelle_, Tom. IV.<x_0.5557><y_0.6562><class_Caption>

<x_0.8027><y_0.0102>S03<x_0.8799><y_0.0273><class_Page-header>

<x_0.7461><y_0.0328>Bilfinger.<x_0.8613><y_0.0469><class_Caption>
